title: The planning agent writes the name when it proposes the node
name: The planning agent writes the name when
description:
`propose` and `open_node` in packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts take `title`, `description`, `files`, `dependsOn` and `decisions`. Nothing asks the agent for a short name, so a board planned today gets whatever the decision's fallback produces rather than a name somebody chose.

Add it to both tool inputs, and to the plan skill so the agent knows what a good one is: a handle, two to four words, distinct from its siblings on the board — `run-panel`, `log-wire`, `readme-guide` — not a compressed restatement of the title and not a category word that three nodes could share. The title stays the sentence; the name is what a person says out loud when they mean this node.

The skill source is plugins/skills/plan/SKILL.md, not the copy under packages/*-plugin/skills/. Those are generated by scripts/build-plugins.mjs; edit the source, run `pnpm plugins`, and commit the regenerated output, or test/integration/plugin.test.ts fails and the next build reverts the hand-edit.

If the decision below makes the name derived rather than written, this node shrinks to the skill wording alone — and it still has to happen, because an agent that writes a 90-character title is what makes a derived name unreadable too.

brief.approach:
Score 3: one input field on one tool, plus the skill prose that decides whether the field gets a good value. Small, and the prose is the part that matters.

**Read what already landed.** `a-node-gets-a-short-name-a-person-can-re-xygw` merged: `Node.name` is a required `z.string().min(1).max(40)` (`packages/schema/src/node.ts`), `createNode` in `packages/core/src/flag.ts` takes `opening.name` and falls back to `shortName(title)`, ids are now seeded from the name, and the `open_node` tool in `packages/mcp/src/tools/flag.ts` already takes `name` with a `.describe()`. So **`open_node` is done** — check it before touching it and leave it alone.

**What is left is `propose`.** `NodeInput` in `packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts` (~line 45) has `key`, `title`, `description`, `files`, `dependsOn`, `decisions` and no `name`, so every node from a planning session gets the derived fallback rather than a name somebody chose. Add it, matching the shape `open_node` already uses so the two tools do not describe the same field two ways:

```ts
name: z.string().min(1).max(40).describe('a short name a person tells this node from its siblings by, like `log-wire`'),
```

Required, not optional. The accepted decision is that somebody chooses it, and an optional field is one every agent will skip. Pass it through to `createNode` (or to whatever `propose` uses to build the record — it writes nodes directly with `writeNode`, so follow that path and set `name` on the record, and seed the id from the name the way `createNode` does, so a proposed node's id is no worse than an opened one's).

**The skill — `plugins/skills/plan/SKILL.md`.** The step that decomposes into nodes lists what each node needs; add the name to that list with what a good one is, in two or three sentences:

- a handle, two to four words — `run-panel`, `log-wire`, `readme-guide`;
- distinct from its **siblings on the board**, which is the whole job: a category word three nodes could share is worse than no name, and `a-new-node-is-checked-against-the-nodes-0ny5` already makes the agent look at what is on the board, so this is a use for what it is already reading;
- not a compressed restatement of the title. The title stays the sentence; the name is what a person says out loud when they mean this node.

Say the thing the node's own text points at: an agent that writes a 90-character title makes even a derived name unreadable, so the naming advice is load-bearing whether or not the field is written by hand.

Then `pnpm plugins` and commit the four regenerated copies with the source. `test/integration/plugin.test.ts` is the drift check; never hand-edit a generated copy.

**Tests.** In `test/integration/mcp.test.ts`, extend the existing `propose` cases: a proposal carrying names writes them onto the records and seeds each id from its name; a proposal missing one is refused by the tool's own schema rather than silently defaulted. Do not start a new test file.

Nothing else changes: no schema move (the field exists), no core change, no CLI, no dashboard.

acceptance.proves: propose takes a name, writes it onto the record and seeds the id from it, and a proposal with no name is refused by the tool's schema instead of quietly falling back to a derived one
the four generated plan skills match the source after `pnpm plugins`, so the naming advice reaches every host

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'name' -- packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts && git grep -q 'log-wire' -- plugins/skills/plan/SKILL.md
acceptance.proves: the field is on the tool and the skill says what a good name looks like with a real example rather than an abstract rule

acceptance.run: test -z "$(git diff --name-only development -- packages/schema packages/core packages/cli apps)"
acceptance.proves: the schema, core, the CLI and the dashboard are untouched — the field already exists and this node only asks the agent for it
the widened NodeInput and its use at the write site compile
